title: ordinal() gives wrong suffix for negative integers (-1 -> '-1th')
property: the ordinal suffix of -n depends on the digits of n, same as for n (1->st, 2->nd, 3->rd, 11-13->th)
evidence: Docstring: 'Works for any integer'; 1 is '1st', 2 is '2nd', 3 is '3rd'. The code uses Python's modulo (value % 10, value % 100) on a negative value, which yields 9/8/7 etc., so the suffix is chosen from the wrong digit.
